commit.message:
Keep the UTC offset in Time#change for times with a zone object

Time#change built the new time with Time.new(..., zone) and then moved
it to the second occurrence of a repeated hour when that matched the
original offset. For a TZInfo::Timezone with TZInfo's default
ambiguity settings, Time.new raises TZInfo::AmbiguousTime for a local
time in the repeated hour, so change(nsec:), change(hour:) and Active
Model's datetime cast, when precision truncation is needed, raised
there. Where the zone picks the other occurrence, as
ActiveSupport::TimeZone does for Europe/Dublin (whose winter time
counts as DST), the original offset was missed and change returned a
time one hour later.

It now tries the original UTC offset first and keeps it when the zone
gives that offset for the new local time, which is the occurrence
change already meant to pick, and builds the time from the zone as
before otherwise. When neither occurrence of the new local time has
the original offset, the zone picks as before, so a TZInfo zone still
raises there; a time in a skipped hour still raises as before.

commit.message:
Let a temporary SQLite table or view hide a permanent one in the schema readers

The batched schema readers listed every row of sqlite_master and
sqlite_temp_master. When a temporary table had the name of a permanent
one, both rows matched, and the pragmas resolved both names to the
temporary table, so columns and indexes came back twice and the primary
key became composite. List a permanent table or view only when no
temporary table or view has its name, as SQLite does when it resolves a
name. Temporary indexes and triggers take no part in that, so they hide
nothing.

commit.message:
Skip merging a blank relation into a relation without conditions

Association#target_scope merges klass.scope_for_association into every
association scope it builds. For a model without a default scope that
isn't an STI subclass, that relation has no values, and the
AssociationRelation it is merged into has no conditions yet. The Merger
still goes through every value and merges the where and having clauses,
which allocates a new WhereClause and its arrays.

Return early when the other relation has no values and the receiver has
no where or having conditions. A receiver with conditions keeps going
through the merge, because WhereClause#merge also drops its duplicate
predicates. A relation whose values were removed with except or only can
still be null, so that case keeps going through the merge too, which
makes the receiver null.

commit.message:
Don't compare owner conditions when joining an association without a scope

To detect conditions that the association scope removed, join_scope
subtracts where clauses before and after merging the scope items, also
when there are none. Comparing predicates can call into their bind
values: Array#- hashes both sides once they are large enough, and
QueryAttribute#hash and #== serialize the value. So a join whose target
default scope has an out of range condition raised
ActiveModel::RangeError instead of matching no records.

Skip the comparison when the association has no scope items, since
nothing can have removed a condition.

Allocate less per field in text_field_tag and tag

Follow-up to #50312: each param of `button_to` goes through
`hidden_field_tag(name, value, id: nil)` and `text_field_tag`, which
computed an id with `sanitize_to_id` only for `id: nil` to drop it.

`text_field_tag` now computes the id only when the options have none,
so a name that `sanitize_to_id` can't convert, such as one with invalid
UTF-8, no longer raises when an `id` is given. `sanitize_to_id` replaces
characters in its first copy instead of making a second, and `tag`
freezes its string before `html_safe`, as `content_tag_string` and
`self_closing_tag_string` already do, so the SafeBuffer can share it
without Ruby allocating a hidden string for both to share.

Honor DATE_FORMATS overrides of built-in formats

lookup preferred the frozen registry whenever the key already existed,
so Time::DATE_FORMATS[:short] = "..." and the Date equivalent did not

deprecated override of the same name.

and a non-main Ractor keeps the built-in format when that snapshot
cannot be shared, so to_fs of other formats keeps working.

commit.message:
Give Live actions the event reporter context and tags of their request

Rails.event context and tags live in Fiber storage, which a new thread
copies from the thread that creates it. ActionController::Live runs
actions on a cached thread pool, so a pool thread kept the context of
the request that created it for its whole life, and the executor reset
runs on the request thread, not on the pool thread. Events from later
Live actions on that thread got another request's context, for example
another user's id, and context set on the request thread was missing.

Capture the context and tags when the action is handed to the pool, set
exactly those on the pool thread, and clear the context when the action
is done.

commit.message:
Don't run a query when checking `or` compatibility

`Relation#or` and `#and` compare both relations' structural values
with `==`. When `from` holds an association relation, its `==` is
`other == records`, so the check loads that relation just to build
the combined relation:

    relation = Post.from(author.posts.select(Arel.star), "posts")
    relation.where(id: 1).or(relation.where(id: 2))
    # => SELECT "posts".* FROM "posts" WHERE "posts"."author_id" = ?

Both sides usually come from the same base relation and share the
same value object, so skip `==` when the values are identical.

commit.message:
Stop setting the Action Mailer delivery job in load_defaults

Action Mailer falls back to ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob itself since
Active Job became optional for it, but the 6.0 defaults still set the
same class by name. The railtie constantizes it when Action Mailer
loads, which requires Active Job, so an app with actionmailer and
without activejob raised LoadError at boot.

Add `change_check_constraint` for PostgreSQL 19+

PostgreSQL 19 extends `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... [NOT] ENFORCED`
from foreign key constraints to check constraints. `change_check_constraint`
uses it to change an existing check constraint between `ENFORCED` and
`NOT ENFORCED`, as `change_foreign_key` does for foreign keys.

https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/19.0/#RELEASE-19-CONSTRAINTS

Changing a constraint to `ENFORCED` checks all existing rows and the
constraint becomes validated. Changing it to `NOT ENFORCED` makes it not
validated.

Like `change_foreign_key`, it is not registered in the migration command
recorder.

commit.message:
Add `enforced:` option to `add_check_constraint` on PostgreSQL 18+

PostgreSQL 18 adds `NOT ENFORCED` to CHECK constraints. Rails already
supports it for foreign keys, but check constraints had no way to use it.

The floor is 18.0, not 18.4 as for foreign keys. The 18.4 fix is about
DEFERRABLE foreign keys, and PostgreSQL rejects DEFERRABLE on CHECK
constraints.

PostgreSQL stores `NOT ENFORCED` constraints as not valid, so the schema
dumper writes `validate: false, enforced: false` after the table.
`enforced: false, validate: true` is accepted, as it is for
`add_foreign_key`. `validate:` defaults to true, so `enforced: false`
alone generates the same SQL, and PostgreSQL stores the constraint as
not valid without raising an error.

The version check raises for any `enforced:` key, `enforced: true`
included. `add_foreign_key` does the same, and the two stay consistent.

commit.message:
Apply the rest of the scope of a `disable_joins` association

Lazily loading a `disable_joins` association applied only the conditions
and order of its scope, so its other values, such as `select`, `limit`,
`includes`, `readonly`, and `strict_loading`, were lost:

```ruby
class Author < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :posts
  has_many :latest_comments, -> { order(id: :desc).limit(3) }, through: :posts, source: :comments, disable_joins: true
end

Author.first.latest_comments.size
# => all the comments of the author's posts, instead of 3
```

`AssociationScope` merges the rest of the association's own scope into
the query, except `where`, `includes`, `unscope`, and `order`, which it
handles by itself. `DisableJoinsAssociationScope` now does the same for
the query of the last link, which is the one that loads the records, and
adds the `includes` there in the same way, so those values apply as they
do without `disable_joins`.

When the last link is put in the order of the previous one in Ruby, the
values are carried over to that relation too, except the order,
`limit`/`offset`, which would cut the records before they are reordered,
`select`, which could leave out the key the records are grouped by, and
`unscope`, which is already applied and would remove the key conditions.

commit.message:
Fix preloading ordered `has_many :through` scoped on its through table

Preloading a through association whose scope has a hash condition on
the through table lost the order of the scope when the order is given
as a Symbol, a Hash or an Arel attribute:

    class Author < ApplicationRecord
      has_many :categorizations
      has_many :special_categories,
        -> { where(categorizations: { special: true }).order(:name) },
        through: :categorizations, source: :category
    end

    author.special_categories.map(&:name)
    # => ["Cooking", "General", "Technology"]

    Author.preload(:special_categories).find(author.id)
      .special_categories.map(&:name)
    # => ["General", "Cooking", "Technology"]

A `has_one :through` with such a scope returned another record than
when it is loaded lazily, and a scope that also has a hash condition on
the source table raised `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid`.

The through query applies the conditions and the order of the scope, so
the source table has to be joined in it. It is now joined whenever the
scope has conditions, as it already was for conditions given as an SQL
string. A scope with hash conditions on the through table only is
loaded with that join as well, instead of a separate query for the
source records.

The order of a scope on its own table stopped counting as a reference
to the source table in 63cf73e451, which is not in a release. A scope
with hash conditions on both tables and no order raised before that
too.

Locate an Array of records passed to a job with one query per model

Active Job deserialized each Global ID on its own, so a job given 100

commit.message:
Check the encrypted file key length when decrypting

`ActiveSupport::EncryptedFile` only checked the key length when
encrypting. Because `[key].pack("H*")` pads an odd-length hex key with a
0 nibble, a 32-character key ending in `0` that lost its last character
still decrypted the file. Apps booted with such a key, while
`credentials:edit` and `encrypted:edit` opened the editor and then raised
`InvalidKeyLengthError` on save, losing the edits.

The length is now checked when the encryptor is built, so reading and
writing both raise `InvalidKeyLengthError`, including for keys that are
too short (previously OpenSSL's `ArgumentError`). Comma-separated keys
are checked one by one. `key?` still only reports presence.

The credentials and encrypted commands print a readable error for
`InvalidKeyLengthError`, and the edit commands fail before opening the
editor. `credentials:diff` falls back to printing the encrypted file, as
it does for `InvalidMessage`, so `git diff` keeps working.

commit.message:
Don't extract a table name starting with a digit from an SQL literal

The previous commit stopped extracting a reference from an SQL literal
wrapped in an `Ordering`, which also stopped extracting it from an SQL
literal used as a hash key, since both are built into the same node:

```ruby
Post.includes(:comments).order(Arel.sql("comments.body") => :desc).to_a
# => no such column: comments.body
```

The `"1"` extracted from `Arel.sql("1.0 * posts.tags_count").desc` came
from `extract_table_name_from` taking a leading number as a table name,
which also happens for an SQL literal without a direction. Instead of
skipping SQL literal orderings, don't take a name starting with a digit
as a table name, so `Arel.sql("comments.body").desc` and
`Arel.sql("comments.body") => :desc` reference `comments`, while
`Arel.sql("1.0 * posts.tags_count")` with or without a direction does
not add a reference.

commit.message:
Rescue all Redis errors in RedisCacheStore failsafe

The RedisCacheStore built on redis-client (#57004) only rescued
`RedisClient::ConnectionError` in `failsafe`, while the previous store
also rescued command errors (#57476). So when Redis returned an error
such as OOM (`maxmemory` with the `noeviction` policy), a wrong
password or `WRONGTYPE`, every cache read and write raised instead of
being treated as a miss and reported to the `error_handler`.

Rescue `RedisClient::Error`, and test the failsafe with a command error,
since the existing tests only raise connection errors.

commit.message:
Speed up numbering of Action Text plain-text list items

Since #55025 the position of an `<li>` in an `<ol>` is found with
`node.parent.elements.index(node)`. That builds a NodeSet of all the
parent's element children and scans it in Ruby, once for every `<li>`.

Count the preceding sibling elements in libxml instead. For a flat list
of 20,000 items, `PlainTextConversion.node_to_plain_text` goes from about
22 seconds to about 1.7 seconds (Ruby 3.4.12, Linux, Nokogiri 1.19.6).

This is still quadratic in the number of items, but the per-item work is
done in C rather than in Ruby. The output is unchanged.

commit.message:
Match Rack::BadRequest errors in ActionDispatch::ParamError

ActionDispatch::Request#POST converts ActionDispatch::ParamError into
ActionController::BadRequest, but ParamError.=== only matched three
explicit Rack error classes. Other malformed-body errors that Rack tags
with Rack::BadRequest, such as Rack::Multipart::BoundaryTooLongError or
MultipartPartLimitError, escaped as 500s instead of 400s.

Match Rack::BadRequest when it is defined (Rack >= 3.1) and keep the
explicit classes for Rack 3.0.

commit.message:
Look up an existing connection lease without the registry mutex

Since #59844, LeaseRegistry#lease takes a mutex on every call, so every
lease_connection, with_connection and active_connection? does too. The
mutex only needs to cover creating a lease, so that a new lease gets the
terminated flag of the registry it is stored in. A lease that is already
there is returned the same way the locked lookup would return it before a
concurrent clear, which marks it terminated as before.

Keep adapter-specific index readers on every IndexDefinition

#59850 moved lengths, opclasses, type, include and nulls_not_distinct
into the MySQL and PostgreSQL index definitions. Code shared across
adapters reads them on any index: migration helpers that recreate an
index (GitLab, Mastodon, online_migrations) read lengths on PostgreSQL,
and active_record_doctor reads type. On main those raise NoMethodError.
Define them on the abstract class with the values 8.1 returned there,
and let the adapters keep overriding them.

Hide generator-only flags from `rails new --help`

`AppGenerator` inherits `--skip-namespace` and `--skip-collision-check`
from `Rails::Generators::Base`. Both flags are intended for generators
run inside an existing application or engine.

Keep accepting both flags for compatibility with existing invocations
and custom application templates.

commit.message:
Don't build log subscriber events whose logging is turned off

Some ActionController::LogSubscriber handlers return early when a setting
turns their logging off: fragment_cache with enable_fragment_cache_logging,
and the three CSRF events with log_warning_on_csrf_failure. consumes? didn't
know about these settings, so the event reporter still built each event
(tags, context, caller locations) for it to be thrown away. With Russian
doll caching that is one unused event per fragment.

event_log_level now takes an if: condition, checked by both emit and
consumes?, and these handlers use it instead of returning early. The
structured subscriber also checks emitting? before expanding the fragment
cache key.

commit.message:
Limit the size of the quoted name caches

The SQLite3, MySQL and PostgreSQL adapters cache every column and table
name they quote, in process-wide maps that are never cleared. Most names
come from the schema, but some come from user input, for example
`order(params[:sort] => :asc)` or `where(params[:field] => value)`. The
name is quoted before the database rejects an unknown column, so each
unique value stays in memory for the life of the process.

Stop caching new names once a cache holds 1,000 entries. Names that are
already cached are still returned from the cache, and other names are
quoted on each call.

commit.message:
Deprecate a positional table name in Arel::Table.new

which Rails 8.1 and earlier accept, now raises ArgumentError. Arel is
private API, but gems and apps call it: flipper 1.4.2, Discourse and
Docuseal among them.

The positional name keeps working with a deprecation warning and
behaves exactly as name:. A call passing both uses the positional name;
neither the Rails 8.1 signature nor main's allows both. The deprecator's
dependency is required, so this also works when Arel is loaded on its own.

Don't share nested values of a column default between records

Column defaults are now cast and frozen once per model, and a new record
gets a `dup` of the default value. The `dup` is shallow, so a nested Hash
or Array of a json, jsonb or PostgreSQL array default was the same object
for every record: changing it in place on one record changed the default
for every record built after it.

A record now gets a `deep_dup` of a frozen default.
